title: Container harness run record (C10)
description: The sanitized, TRACKED summary the host-side driver derives from a run's ephemeral runs/<utc>/<row-id>/ bundle. A green host-lane row is the only evidence that promotes a hosts/capabilities.yaml field from `documented` to `verified`, and evidence a reviewer cannot open at the promotion commit — or that `make e2e-clean` erases — cannot back a claim that ships to users. So this file is committed alongside the promotion while the raw bundle stays gitignored and prunable. The writer refuses any key outside this schema, so 'the driver learned to log one more field' cannot quietly turn a record into a transcript.

started_at.description: UTC ISO-8601; matches the <utc> segment of the bundle directory.

creds_mode.description: The operator's choice for the whole invocation. NOT the same thing as a host's recorded credential_mode, which is Phase 1's measurement that no working credential path was found for that host.

egress.description: Recorded so a row's evidence states which guarantee it had: `none` is structural (a mis-redirected CLI cannot reach a real endpoint), `open` is detection-only, `allowlist` converts detection back into a structural guarantee.

route.description: Which install route this row exercised: `file` for a shim `install-host` wrote, `package` for a distribution the host's own installer resolved. Absent means `file`, which is what every row recorded before a package route existed. It is what keys promotion: a `package` row writes no shim, so crediting it with `shim`/`install_paths`/`arguments`/`reload` would describe a file at a path the row never touched.

model.description: The PINNED slug from host_matrix.yaml, never a run-time 'cheapest' lookup.

reason.description: Named reason on a skip/fail/cap-hit — e.g. `cap-hit: tool-loop`, `cap-hit: no-first-call`, `cap-hit: stalled-after-<turn>`, `not_authenticated`, `permission`. Also carries the GRADER's side of the verdict on an otherwise green row: `provisional` (the record was written when the row exited, before pytest graded it — such a record proposes no promotion), `ungraded` (no test ever asserted on this row), or the assertion that failed it. A row whose container exited 0 but whose assertions failed is recorded `fail` and names them here.

write_outcome.description: The worst outcome any of this row's write batches recorded, in the schema's own spelling of the product's D3g vocabulary (the map is `harness.WRITE_OUTCOME_SEVERITY`). Absent means the row dispatched no write batch at all — never that its batches did nothing, which is what `no-op` says: the runner claimed there was nothing to apply and the pre/post byte comparison agreed. `no-op` was added 2026-09-22, after `1633dd4` (2026-09-16) split the classifier's empty-diff branch and made it this rig's MOST COMMON write outcome (65 of 65 batches in `runs/20260921T224840Z`); before that split the same batches were classified `clean-failure`, which is why records older than it spell an honest no-op that way. `policy-violation` has no spelling here on purpose — see `harness.WRITE_OUTCOME_SEVERITY` — and reaches the record through `rows[].reason`.

actual_usd.description: null means the readback surfaces did not answer; the running total is then relabelled `estimate` rather than `spend` and the record says actual: unavailable. A number is never recorded that was not measured.

next_command.description: T10 of plans/next-phase-command.md, on a `next_command_check` row only: what the host did with the command its dispatcher printed. Derived from the bundle by `next_command_check.observe` (the function the row's tests assert on) and summarized by `record_block`. `printed_*` are the dispatcher's own `user_next_step`, read from the session's receipts. `copied` is criterion 4 — the final assistant message carries `printed_command` and every `printed_optional` as fenced lines, byte for byte — and is null when nothing was printed; `copied_unfenced` says the command appeared only outside a fence. `lookup` and `stop_hook` are claude-code's two extras. `no_call` is criterion 5 on the tool routes, null when no tool result handed the model a `user_next_step`. `typed` is the typed-template check: a fresh session handed the printed command verbatim.

model.description: The slug the host session really ran, from the bundle's credential census: an operator's `MLLM_HOST_MODEL` override when there was one. The row's `model` column keeps the checked-in pin.

route_observed.description: The `next_command` route key whose template prefix the printed command starts with.

census.description: How many hosts ran in each mode, each named with its reason. `3/0/0/0` and `0/0/3/0` are both possible outcomes of the same command, and a summary that cannot tell them apart is exactly how zero host coverage passes for a green matrix.

bundle.description: Digests of the ephemeral half, so the deletable bundle stays checkable without being durable. If the operator still has it, `make e2e-verify-record` re-hashes and says whether it is the one the promotion cited; if it is gone, the record still stands on its own and the reviewer knows precisely what is no longer inspectable.

archive_url.description: Optional. The digest is what is trusted; the URL is only how you fetch the bytes.

promotions.description: The hosts/capabilities.yaml edits this run justifies. PRINTED, never applied: promoting a capability changes which code path ships to users, so it stays a human commit carrying the record file and the capabilities edit in the same diff. An entry here means the row passed TWICE — its container exited 0 and the assertions over its bundle passed. A record written before the grader ran, or for a row the grader failed or never looked at, carries an empty array and says which in `rows[].reason`.
